title: Winning tickets from large natural-image source datasets transfer across natural-image target datasets with near target-specific performance
content: Winning-ticket initializations discovered by iterative magnitude pruning (iterative pruning rate 0.2, up to 30 pruning iterations; late resetting to early training iterations) on large, complex natural-image source datasets (ImageNet and Places365, and to a lesser extent CIFAR-100) produce sparse initializations that, when used to train a VGG19 or ResNet50 architecture on other natural-image target datasets (SVHN, Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, ImageNet, Places365), frequently achieve test accuracies on the target tasks that are close to the accuracies obtained by winning tickets discovered directly on those target datasets. The transferability is observed across a wide range of pruning fractions (including very high sparsity), and larger / more class-rich source datasets produced stronger cross-dataset transfer than smaller sources (e.g., CIFAR-100 tickets generalize better than CIFAR-10 tickets despite both having 50,000 training examples).

title: Source dataset scale and number of classes predict transferability of winning tickets
content: Winning tickets discovered on larger source datasets—both in terms of number of training examples and number of output classes—transfer substantially better to other natural-image classification datasets (SVHN, Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, ImageNet, Places365) than tickets discovered on smaller source datasets, for both VGG19 and ResNet50 architectures. This effect is not solely explained by raw training-set size: holding training-set size fixed, a source dataset with many classes (CIFAR-100, 100 classes) produced tickets that generalized better across targets than one with few classes (CIFAR-10, 10 classes).

title: Winning tickets can generalize across optimizers (SGD w/ momentum and Adam) for VGG models
content: Winning-ticket initializations generated with one optimizer generalize to training with a different optimizer on natural-image classification datasets: VGG19 tickets found using SGD with momentum or using Adam, when re-used with the alternate optimizer, achieve high performance that is comparable to tickets discovered under the target optimizer. There are optimizer-dependent nuances in behavior: tickets transferred from SGD to Adam sometimes under-perform random tickets at low pruning fractions but outperform random tickets at high pruning fractions.

title: Winning tickets generalize across different samples from the same data distribution
content: A winning ticket discovered on CIFAR-10a, a subset of the CIFAR-10 dataset containing 25,000 training images with 2,500 images per class, transfers to a disjoint subset CIFAR-10b from the same data distribution and improves training on that held-out subset relative to random sparse initializations. This within-distribution transfer holds for both VGG19 and ResNet50, though ResNet50 showed sensitivity at low pruning fractions (occasionally under-performing random tickets when few weights are pruned).

title: Global magnitude pruning outperforms layerwise pruning and results in non-uniform layerwise sparsity (deeper layers pruned more) under global schedules
content: When performing magnitude pruning for winning-ticket discovery on VGG19 trained on CIFAR-10, globally ranking weights across all layers and pruning the smallest-magnitude weights globally yields higher-performing sparse subnetworks than pruning a fixed fraction per layer ("layerwise pruning"). Under global magnitude pruning the pruning fractions vary across layers: deeper convolutional layers are pruned more heavily while early layers (notably the first convolutional layer) retain a much larger fraction of their parameters.

title: Mask structure carries substantial information; fair random baselines must randomize mask structure
content: For VGG19 trained on CIFAR-10, the structure of the pruning mask contains substantial information useful for training sparse networks: comparing (a) preserved winning-ticket masks, (b) masks permuted only within layers (local permutation), and (c) masks permuted across all layers (global permutation) shows that locally permuting a mask degrades performance moderately while globally permuting the mask degrades performance dramatically. Therefore, a fair "random ticket" baseline for evaluating a winning-ticket initialization should randomize both weight values and mask structure (global permutation), because preserving mask statistics across layers transfers information from the discovered ticket.

title: Late resetting and iterative magnitude-pruning schedule used to obtain winning tickets for large models and datasets
content: For obtaining competitive winning tickets in the large-model and large-dataset regime of natural-image classification, an iterative magnitude-pruning schedule with pruning fraction per iteration 0.2 (20% of remaining parameters) over up to 30 iterations combined with late resetting to parameters at a small early training iteration produced effective winning tickets; late resetting settings used were resetting to the parameters after 1 epoch for Fashion-MNIST, SVHN, CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, and after 3 epochs for ImageNet and Places365. Learning-rate annealing schedules and other hyperparameters were matched per model family (VGG19 trained 160 epochs with LR drops at epochs 80 and 120; ResNet50 trained 90 epochs with LR drops at epochs 50, 65, and 80).
